text: Now let's give these events a real home — Eventhouse and KQL Database.

An Eventhouse holds one or more KQL databases — the same containing relationship a workspace has to its items, just scoped to real-time data. New item, Eventhouse, name it — the same shape as every other item so far.

And it's genuinely optimized differently from a Delta table. Delta is built around versioned, transactional writes. A KQL database is built for extreme ingestion rates, queryable within seconds — neither one is better, they solve different problems, exactly like last chapter's lakehouse versus warehouse decision.

And this is the real connection point back to Lesson 19 — an eventstream's eventhouse destination actually targets one specific KQL database and table. Events flow from a source, through transformations, and land here as real, queryable rows.
A container, a real storage engine, purpose-built for streaming. Next lesson: what is KQL, the language that actually queries it.
